narrative_purpose: Illustrates the chapter's central paradox: a small old world should look like a dead grey cratered moon, yet Pandora is still molten. Two moons side by side make the contrast between expected death and observed life.
subject: Two moons side by side in space against a starfield. On the left, a grey, cratered, geologically dead world with a frozen cracked crust and no glow - the fate a small world expects. On the right, a moon of similar size still faintly threaded with glowing orange molten fractures, subtly alive. A clear gap of dark space separates them so they read as a comparison pair.
scene: Deep space, two moons floating at the same scale on a shared dark starfield, nothing else competing.
camera: Balanced two-up composition, both moons at equal size for direct comparison, centered.
light: Left moon lit only by cold flat starlight, grey and lifeless; right moon self-lit by scarce warm ember-amber glow from its molten seams; deep indigo void between.
palette: Left moon desaturated grey-indigo; right moon cool dark crust with scarce ember-amber fracture glow; void-indigo background.
style: Painterly astronomical plate, naturalistic cratered and fractured surfaces.
detail_level: Crisp craters on the dead moon and glowing seams on the live moon; background soft dark haze.
composition: Two moons on left and right thirds with a dark gap between, equal size, generous dark negative space.
consistency_notes: The live moon on the right should match Pandora's dark-crust-with-amber-seams look from the cover. The dead moon reads clearly as grey and lifeless for contrast.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon style
